security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, placeholder URLs, or documented token-storage text rather than malicious behavior. The skill does intentionally ask users to install and run the RunComfy CLI, so external command use is confirmed and should require explicit user consent.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before npm, npx, or runcomfy commands. Pin or verify the RunComfy CLI package where possible.
Tell users before sending prompts, image URLs, audio URLs, or video URLs to RunComfy model services.
Do not print tokens. Keep token files owner-only and prefer scoped RUNCOMFY_TOKEN values in CI.

content.user_title: Animate Images with RunComfy Video Models
content.value_statement: Still images need the right model and prompt to become useful video clips. This skill routes image-to-video requests to RunComfy models with matching settings and examples.
actual_capabilities: Routes general image animation requests to HappyHorse 1.0 I2V.
Routes custom voiceover lip-sync requests to Wan 2.7 with audio input.
Routes multimodal image, video, and audio reference requests to Seedance 2.0 Pro.
Lists model parameters, media limits, durations, aspect ratios, and resolutions.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocation examples and prompt-writing guidance.
Explains token storage, outbound endpoints, and generated file size limits.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and valid authentication.
Sends prompts and media URLs to RunComfy for remote processing.
Cannot combine multiple routes in one call; use separate calls for mixed workflows.
Each model keeps its own duration, media size, resolution, and aspect-ratio limits.

use_cases.title: Create Product Motion Clips
use_cases.description: Turn product photos into short reveal videos with camera movement and stable packaging details.

use_cases.title: Animate Portraits for Social Posts
use_cases.description: Convert a portrait image into a brief clip with facial stability, subtle motion, and optional ambient audio.

use_cases.title: Produce Localized Talking Clips
use_cases.description: Use the same visual concept with different voiceover tracks for multilingual lip-sync variants.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Single Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a basic image-to-video clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this image into a 5 second video. Keep the subject stable and add a gentle camera push-in.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Product Reveal
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with motion and preservation goals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this product photo into a 6 second reveal video. Orbit slowly, keep labels readable, and preserve packaging geometry.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Lip-Sync Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using a custom voiceover URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 12 second talking-head video from this portrait and voiceover. Match the duration, use warm studio light, and avoid subtitles.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multimodal Reference Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using image, video, and audio references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image 1 for the subject, video 1 for scene movement, and audio 1 for voice tone. Produce an 8 second cinematic clip.

output_examples.input: A user provides a product photo and asks for a short vertical launch teaser.
output_examples.output: The skill selects HappyHorse 1.0 I2V, recommends a portrait aspect workflow, and drafts a motion-focused product reveal prompt.

output_examples.input: A user has a portrait image and a 10 second voiceover for a spokesperson clip.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Wan 2.7 with audio input, aligns duration to the voiceover, and suggests a stable talking-head prompt.

output_examples.input: A user wants a subject photo animated with a reference cafe video and a voice reference.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Seedance 2.0 Pro and explains how to map each reference to subject, scene, and voice behavior.

best_practices: State the primary motion first, then describe camera movement, lighting changes, and preservation goals.
Match duration to the source audio when generating lip-sync or voice-led clips.
Confirm users have rights to submit any image, video, or audio URL to RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Do not use one prompt to request several unrelated motions in a short clip.
Do not submit private media URLs without user consent and access review.
Do not assume one model supports every route, reference type, or output resolution.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to submit requests to RunComfy model services.

faq.question: Which model is used by default?
faq.answer: HappyHorse 1.0 I2V is the default for general portrait, product, and image animation requests.

faq.question: Can it use a custom voiceover?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes custom voiceover lip-sync requests to Wan 2.7 with an audio URL.

faq.question: Can it use reference video and audio together?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes image, video, and audio reference workflows to Seedance 2.0 Pro.

faq.question: What authentication is required?
faq.answer: Users need the RunComfy CLI and either a RunComfy login session or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: What should users check before running it?
faq.answer: Users should verify media rights, media size limits, model duration limits, and consent for third-party processing.
